title: Opal Systems: pen test debrief & patch cadence orchestration
summary: Debrief of the external pentest findings and agreement on a pragmatic patch cadence and SDLC hardening plan. Discussed SOC 2 scoping, K M S integration options, RBAC/SSO alignment, and audit log retention. Agreed to run a short benchmark on Redwood Dedicat under a controlled workload and to share security pack and timeline for remediation steps.
topics: Patch cadence and emergency hotfix SLA
RBAC, SSO/SAML integration and least privilege
Encryption at rest and K M S integration options
Audit logs, retention, and access controls
SOC 2 evidence mapping and gap items
Pilot for private deployment / V P C networking
action_items: Jonah - produce triage spreadsheet mapping pentest findings to remediation owners and estimated effort (due 2026-11-25)
Maya - send security whitepaper, SOC 2 attestation stub, and K M S integration doc (due 2026-11-20)
Priya - share internal risk matrix and confirm which findings they want treated as release blockers (due 2026-11-22)
Tom - schedule a sandbox test window for Redwood Dedicat performance/prefix cache test (proposed 2026-11-30)
Raj - confirm decision maker list for emergency patch SLA signoff (due 2026-11-24)
next_steps: Redwood to share pen-test mapping spreadsheet and security pack
Customer to confirm blocker list and priority for hotfixes
Schedule 2-hour technical deep-dive next week for K M S and V P C routing
Set up pilot for 2-week Dedicated capacity benchmark
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-18 09:23 UTC | Duration 62m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Priya (Opal Sr Sec Eng), Tom (Opal Platform), Raj (Opal CISO)

Summary: quick debrief from the pentest team, then move into remediation cadence and longer term sdlc controls. Some notes on SOC two evidence and KMS integration options.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we got the pentest results in front of us, i'll let Jonah walk through the technical bits.
00:18 Jonah: cool, thanks Maya. so quick primer — the tester report surfaced 3 critical, 7 high, a handful of medium items. some overlap with creds leakage vectors and a couple of path traversal-ish findings in our file-service endpoints. also flagged a cache key exposure scenario with the K V cache.
00:36 Priya: can you clarify "cache key exposure" — is that the prefix K V cache leak that shows user ids?
00:43 Jonah: yeah it's mostly prefix metadata, not full tokens, but in combination with log sampling it could be used to correlate sessions. tester reproduced with a race condition under heavy load.
00:55 Tom: that race was on their staging variant, not our prod, right?
01:01 Jonah: tester used a load tool against a staging env that mimics Redwood Dedicat config. it's worth noting they had some differences in auth headers; might be a config drift.
01:12 Priya: okay, config drift — we need to know whether this is a code bug or infra misconfig.
01:18 Jonah: initial read is infra config + caching path handling — low level runtime path. we can provide a patch pattern.
01:26 Raj: high level question — for our compliance posture (SOC two) how many of these are considered control failures vs implementation bugs?
01:34 Maya: good Q. from a SOC 2 perspective,Raj, we think the ones tied to access control and auditability map directly to control failures; others are implementation vulnerabilities. We'll put together mapping.
01:48 Priya: on K M S — the report says local key storage for some logs. is that true?
01:55 Jonah: tester saw some logs written leaving PII in clear in a debug path. mainline is encrypted at rest with customer-managed K M S optionality but the debug path was using a local ephemeral store.
02:09 Tom: that debug path is from an old SDK we have in our infra. we'll patch it but need to understand Redwood's rotation policy.
02:16 Jonah: rotation policy: we support rotation via customer K M S and automated key rotation on Redwood Hosted; for Redwood Private customers you plug your H S M — we call out the steps in the K M S integration doc. note: doc may say "K M S" in a couple of places as separate letters because auto-transcription — ignore formatting.
02:35 Priya: for RBAC, the pentest flagged overly permissive service accounts. how granular is Redwood RBAC today?
02:43 Maya: we have role templates and token scopes; for Dedicated and Private you can map to V P C-limited roles and tie to SAML groups. Jonah, want to add?
02:51 Jonah: yeah, we expose an RBAC layer and you can configure service roles to the minimum; however some of the older onboarding tooling created wide-scoped service tokens — that's what the tester abused. we'll provide a migration script.
03:05 Priya: migration script would be great. does it preserve existing session tokens?
03:11 Jonah: it rotates tokens as part of migration — we'll document downtime windows, typically sub-minute token switch but depends on client session cache TTLs.
03:22 Tom: what about audit logs? where are they stored and how long can we retain? the pentest report asked for retention proof.
03:30 Maya: audit logs are written to immutable append-only storage, by default 90 days for hosted, configurable up to multi-year for dedicated/private. we can send retention policy docs and sample log exports for SOC two evidence.
03:45 Raj: can you make sure that the logs include key rotation events and token issuance?
03:51 Jonah: yes we log key management events and token grants; for customer-managed K M S we include K M S metadata and rotation timestamps — though the telemetry label names in the report may differ, we'll provide canonical mapping.
04:05 Priya: the pentester also found an endpoint that returns stack traces when debug headers are present. is that reproducible?
04:14 Jonah: we patched that in the 1.12.3 patch but the staging env the tester hit hadn't pulled that autoscale image. so it's a release pipeline gap — sdlc concern.
04:26 Maya: this is where patch cadence ties to SDLC hygiene. Opal — do you have a quarterly release window or continuous deploy?
04:34 Tom: we do a weekly deploy but some infra bits are on a monthly maintenance cycle — that's probably why staging drifted.
04:41 Maya: ok so we should align emergency hotfixes vs routine patch windows. propose: critical/hotfix SLA for 24–48 hours, high-level within 7 days, medium within 30 days unless blocked by major dependencies.
04:55 Raj: 24–48 for critical is acceptable but we need signoff on who declares "critical".
05:02 Priya: our risk team will define a blocker list, we'll share it.
05:07 Maya: great, action item. Jonah, about remediation — can Redwood provide a temporary mitigations list we can apply if we can't ship a full patch?
05:15 Jonah: yes, a mitigation playbook. things like toggling a feature flag, tightening token TTL, limiting ingress by IP, increasing log sampling. we'll include runbooks.
05:29 Tom: K M S integration — two options we discussed in reading: customer-managed K M S (we manage key IDs) vs Redwood-hosted with rotation. latency or cost impacts?
05:39 Jonah: customer-managed K M S introduces an extra network call on rotation events but not per-token; negligible on steady state. we did some internal benchmarks, we'll share numbers. note: call overhead can vary if your K M S is on-prem behind VPN.
05:53 Priya: for our compliance we need evidence of encryption at rest and attestations. do you have SOC two type 2 or a readiness report?
06:02 Maya: we have a SOC 2 Type II attestation for Hosted and Dedicated controls; for Private deployments the evidence is the control plane reports and the customer is responsible for on-prem controls. we'll send the attestation and a short mapping doc showing where each control maps.
06:20 Raj: we also need SSO/SAML flows — IdP metadata exchange and SP-initiated flows. any gotchas?
06:28 Jonah: we support SAML2 with signed assertions, SP initiated and IdP-initiated flows, and SCIM for user provisioning; quirks: if you have nested groups some claims can be flattened which affects RBAC mapping. we'll include a sample metadata file and mapping template.
06:44 Priya: question on audit logs access: who at Redwood can view customer logs? is it restricted?
06:51 Maya: restricted to a small ops escalation group under RBAC with audited access and just-in-time approval for deeper access. we can add MFA restrictions on that.
07:04 Tom: the pentest asked for proof of vulnerability scanning — do you run SCA and container scanning in your CI?
07:12 Jonah: yes we run SCA, container image scanning, and infra IaC linting; we also do scheduled dependency scanning and a weekly internal vuln sweep. we'll attach pipeline screenshots for evidence.
07:25 Priya: good. can you also include retention of pipeline logs for forensic?
07:31 Jonah: yep we'll include retention policies and export samples.
07:36 Raj: let's talk risk acceptance — some findings are lower priority but would require significant refactors. what's Redwood's stance on recommended mitigations vs accepted risk?
07:46 Maya: we provide a recommended severity mapping and suggested mitigations; final acceptance is with the customer. for Dedicated we can offer compensating controls like tighter network ACLs.
07:56 Priya: regarding the migration script for tokens, will that require an outage window?
08:03 Jonah: usually small window—token TTL dependent; we can orchestrate a rolling rotation with zero downtime for most clients if session TTL is short. we'll document exact steps.
08:14 Tom: operationally, we need a runbook for emergency patching that lists steps, contacts, and rollback plan. can Redwood provide a runbook template?
08:22 Maya: yes, we'll provide a runbook and an escalation tree.
08:27 Priya: who will be our point for the 24–48 hr hotfix response?
08:31 Maya: primary will be Maya as AE for escalation and Jonah as tech lead, with a named SE on-call. we'll include contact matrix.
08:39 Raj: okay final two asks — include proof of immutable logs and include an export of several log events showing key rotations, token grants, and admin actions.
08:50 Jonah: we can generate redacted export artifacts from our audit pipeline and provide hashes for integrity proof.
08:58 Maya: perfect. let's recap next steps.
09:02 Recap (Maya): 1) Jonah -> triage spreadsheet & mitigation playbook (due 11/25). 2) Maya -> send SOC 2 attestation and K M S doc (due 11/20). 3) Opal -> share blocker list (Priya) by 11/22. 4) Tom -> schedule sandbox test week of 11/30. 5) schedule 2-hr deep dive for K M S + V P C next week.
09:26 Priya: sounds good, thanks all.
09:30 Meeting ends.

Notes: transcription includes occasional auto-splitting of acronyms (e.g., "S O C two", "K M S") and mis-attribution of short timestamps. Shared artifacts: link to pentest report (redacted) - https://redwood.example.com/shared/opal-pentest-2026-11-redacted, link to K M S integration doc - https://redwood.example.com/docs/kms-integration, remediation playbook placeholder - will be uploaded to the shared folder.
